answer:
Headline result (approved primary test): Pearson chi-square test of independence between m6A methylation status (significant = Hyper+Hypo vs no sig) and differential expression status (DEG = Up+Down vs no-DEGs), over all 12,754 transcript rows:

  p-value = 2.95e-72  (chi-square = 323.17, df = 1)

The test overwhelmingly rejects independence — m6A methylation status and differential expression status are strongly associated (m6A-significant transcripts are DEGs at ~20.7% vs ~6.2% for m6A-non-significant; odds ratio ≈ 3.94).

Observed 2×2 contingency table (rows = m6A status, cols = DEG status):
                DEG     no-DEGs   | row total
  m6A sig        246        945    |  1,191
  m6A no sig     717     10,846    | 11,563
  col total      963     11,791    | 12,754

Expected counts under independence (all ≫ 5, chi-square valid):
                DEG       no-DEGs
  m6A sig       89.93     1,101.07
  m6A no sig   873.07    10,689.93

Sensitivity checks (clearly labeled, NOT the headline):
  - Yates-corrected chi-square: statistic = 321.10, df = 1, p = 8.32e-72
  - Fisher's exact test (2×2): p = 8.22e-54 (odds ratio = 3.938)
  All sensitivity checks agree in conclusion; the primary reported answer is the uncorrected Pearson chi-square p-value = 2.95e-72.

Caveat (one line, as requested): rows are transcripts, not unique genes — the 12,754 rows map to only 3,117 unique ENSG genes, so the test treats transcript-level rows as units (per the approved plan).

Appendix note (excluded from the deliverable per instruction): a restricted Hyper/Hypo × Up/Down table (106/12/9/119) also shows association, with a minimum expected count of 55.2 (adequate for chi-square); this variant is not part of the answer.

payload.test: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2, collapsed statuses)
payload.caveat: 12,754 transcript rows map to 3,117 unique ENSG genes; test uses transcript-level rows per approved plan
